cls: Long-acting beta2-adrenergic agonist (LABA), inhaled - once-daily maintenance bronchodilator for COPD
pharm: Ultra-long-acting selective beta2-adrenergic agonist that, when inhaled, acts locally on bronchial smooth-muscle beta2-receptors to stimulate adenylyl cyclase and raise intracellular cyclic AMP, producing rapid-onset, 24-hour bronchodilation suitable for once-daily dosing.
quick: 75 mcg (contents of one capsule) inhaled once daily via the NEOHALER device
Not relevant - oral inhalation only; do NOT swallow the capsule
Former Category C; use only if potential benefit justifies fetal risk
Unknown if excreted in human milk; detected in rat milk - use caution
No dosage adjustment needed (negligible renal elimination)
No adjustment in mild-moderate impairment; no data in severe impairment
No specific interaction described in labeling
Heart rate/BP, serum potassium, blood glucose, COPD control, paradoxical bronchospasm
summary: Indacaterol (Arcapta Neohaler) is an inhaled, once-daily long-acting beta2-agonist (LABA) indicated ONLY for the long-term maintenance bronchodilator treatment of airflow obstruction in COPD (chronic bronchitis and/or emphysema). It is delivered as the dry-powder contents of a single 75 mcg capsule inhaled through the NEOHALER device - the capsule is never swallowed. It is NOT a rescue medication: it must not be used for acute bronchospasm or acutely deteriorating COPD, for which a short-acting beta2-agonist should be used. It is NOT indicated for asthma; using a LABA as monotherapy (without an inhaled corticosteroid) in asthma carries an increased risk of asthma-related death (a recognized LABA class effect), and such use is contraindicated. Common effects mirror beta-agonist class effects - cough, oropharyngeal pain, tremor, and possible cardiovascular effects, hypokalemia, and hyperglycemia. No dose adjustment is required for renal or mild-moderate hepatic impairment.
indications: Long-term, once-daily maintenance bronchodilator treatment of airflow obstruction in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), including chronic bronchitis and/or emphysema
Important limitation: NOT indicated to treat acute deteriorations of COPD
Important limitation: NOT indicated for asthma (safety and effectiveness in asthma not established)

admin: For oral inhalation ONLY with the NEOHALER device - capsules must never be swallowed
Remove the capsule from its blister only immediately before use, then place it in the NEOHALER and pierce it once
Inhale rapidly and deeply; a whirring sound and sweet taste confirm a dose was delivered - inspect the capsule and re-inhale if powder remains
Administer once daily at the same time each day; if a dose is missed, take the next dose as soon as remembered but never more than once per 24 hours
Always use the new NEOHALER inhaler supplied with each new prescription; store capsules in the original blister, protected from light and moisture
moa: Indacaterol is a long-acting beta2-adrenergic agonist. When inhaled it acts locally in the lung as a bronchodilator by selectively stimulating beta2-adrenergic receptors on airway smooth muscle. Receptor activation increases intracellular adenylyl cyclase activity, catalyzing conversion of ATP to cyclic-3',5'-adenosine monophosphate (cyclic AMP); elevated cyclic AMP relaxes bronchial smooth muscle and inhibits the release of mediators of immediate hypersensitivity from cells, particularly mast cells. Its high local potency and slow dissociation give a rapid onset yet sustained, 24-hour duration of action permitting once-daily dosing. Although beta2-receptors predominate in bronchial smooth muscle, beta2-receptors also comprise 10-50% of cardiac adrenergic receptors, so even selective beta2-agonists may produce cardiac effects.

absolute: Use of a LABA, including indacaterol, WITHOUT an inhaled corticosteroid in patients with asthma (increased risk of asthma-related death)
Known hypersensitivity to indacaterol or to any of the product ingredients
relative: Cardiovascular disorders, especially coronary insufficiency, arrhythmias, and hypertension
Convulsive disorders, thyrotoxicosis, or unusual sensitivity to sympathomimetic amines
Pre-existing diabetes or hypokalemia (may be aggravated)
Acutely deteriorating COPD - do not initiate in this setting
monitor: COPD control and need for rescue short-acting beta2-agonist
Signs of paradoxical bronchospasm or immediate hypersensitivity

preg: Formerly Pregnancy Category C. There are no adequate and well-controlled studies of indacaterol in pregnant women; in animal studies indacaterol was not teratogenic in rats and rabbits at doses far above the human 75 mcg dose. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus. As with other beta-agonists, indacaterol may interfere with uterine contractility if used during labor.
lact: It is not known whether indacaterol is excreted in human milk. Because many drugs are excreted in human milk and indacaterol has been detected in the milk of lactating rats, caution should be exercised when administering indacaterol to a nursing woman.
renal: Because urinary elimination contributes very little to total body clearance of indacaterol, a dedicated study in renally impaired subjects was not performed and no dosage adjustment is required for renal impairment.
hepatic: Patients with mild and moderate hepatic impairment showed no relevant changes in Cmax or AUC, and protein binding did not differ from healthy controls; no dosage adjustment is needed. Indacaterol has not been studied in subjects with severe hepatic impairment.

major: Other adrenergic drugs (additional sympathomimetics) - may potentiate cardiovascular effects; use with caution
MAO inhibitors, tricyclic antidepressants, and other QTc-prolonging drugs - may potentiate effects on the cardiovascular system; use with extreme caution
Other long-acting beta2-agonists (LABA) - do not co-administer; excessive use can cause clinically significant, potentially fatal cardiovascular effects
moderate: Xanthine derivatives, corticosteroids, and diuretics - may potentiate beta-agonist-induced hypokalemia and/or ECG changes
Non-potassium-sparing diuretics - risk of additive hypokalemia and ECG changes
Beta-adrenergic blockers - may decrease the effectiveness of indacaterol; use only when medically necessary
Strong CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, ritonavir) - increase systemic exposure but not to a degree of safety concern at the 75 mcg dose
interactions.food: Not applicable - the drug is inhaled, not swallowed; the capsule must never be ingested.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction with alcohol is described in the prescribing information.
interactions.diagnostics: Beta2-agonists may lower serum potassium and raise plasma glucose; interpret electrolyte and glucose results accordingly. Beta-agonists can produce ECG changes (T-wave flattening, QTc prolongation, ST-segment depression).

serious: Clinically significant cardiovascular effects (increased pulse, blood pressure, palpitations, arrhythmias)
rare: Immediate hypersensitivity reactions (rash, urticaria, angioedema, pruritus)
emergency: Serious cardiac arrhythmia from excessive beta-adrenergic stimulation

monitoring: Heart rate, blood pressure, and cardiac symptoms
Serum potassium, particularly with concomitant diuretics, xanthines, or steroids
Blood glucose in diabetic or at-risk patients
COPD symptom control and frequency of rescue short-acting beta2-agonist use
Emergence of paradoxical bronchospasm or hypersensitivity after dosing
counsel: This is a once-a-day maintenance inhaler for COPD - it is NOT a rescue inhaler and will not relieve a sudden breathing attack
Never swallow the capsule; place it in the NEOHALER device and breathe it in deeply - keep a fast-acting rescue inhaler with you for sudden symptoms
Do not use this medicine for asthma, and do not use more than one LABA at a time
Take it at the same time every day; if you miss a dose, take your next dose at the usual time - do not double up
Tell your doctor if your breathing suddenly gets worse right after a dose, or if you have chest pain, a racing or pounding heartbeat, tremor, or a rash or swelling
Store the capsules in their sealed blister, away from moisture and light, and use the new inhaler that comes with each prescription
pk: Rapid bronchodilation, typically within ~5 minutes of inhalation (serum Tmax ~15 minutes)
Peak serum concentration ~15 minutes after inhaled dosing
Effective half-life ~40-56 hours; steady state in ~12-15 days
Bronchodilation sustained over 24 hours, supporting once-daily dosing
Store at 25 C (excursions 15-30 C); protect capsules from light and moisture, keep in original blister
pearls: Once-daily LABA for COPD maintenance ONLY - not a rescue medication and not for acute deteriorations
NOT for asthma: LABA monotherapy without an inhaled corticosteroid raises the risk of asthma-related death (class effect)
Capsule is for inhalation via the NEOHALER device - never swallowed
No dose adjustment for renal impairment or mild-moderate hepatic impairment; not studied in severe hepatic impairment
Watch for beta-agonist class effects: hypokalemia, hyperglycemia, tremor, tachycardia, and QTc changes
Do not combine with another LABA - additive cardiovascular toxicity can be fatal
missed: If you miss a dose, take your next dose as soon as you remember, then continue at your usual once-daily time. Do not take more than one dose in any 24-hour period, and never take two doses at once to make up for a missed dose.
overdose: Overdose produces signs of excessive beta-adrenergic stimulation: angina, hypertension or hypotension, tachycardia (rates up to 200 bpm), arrhythmias, nervousness, headache, tremor, dry mouth, palpitations, muscle cramps, nausea, dizziness, fatigue, malaise, hypokalemia, hyperglycemia, and metabolic acidosis. In COPD patients, single doses up to 40 times the 75 mcg dose caused moderate increases in pulse, systolic blood pressure, and QTc. Treatment is discontinuation of the drug plus appropriate symptomatic and supportive therapy; cardioselective beta-blockers may be considered for severe cardiac effects but with caution given the risk of bronchospasm. Cardiac monitoring is advisable.
